The Ganges River. The holiest river in Hinduism and the lifeblood of northern India, flowing approximately twenty-five hundred twenty-five kilometers from the Himalayas southeast across the Indian subcontinent to the Bay of Bengal. Revered as a goddess in Hindu tradition, it sustains over four hundred million people through its vast delta and has shaped Indian spirituality, culture, and civilization for millennia.

The Ganges originates in the Himalayan glaciers and flows southeast through the Ganges Plain, one of the world's most densely populated regions. It is sacred to Hindus as the goddess Ganga. Pilgrims bathe in its waters to cleanse sins and seek divine blessing. Varanasi, built along its banks, is Hinduism's holiest city—where the faithful come to die and be cremated.

The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta in Bangladesh is the world's largest delta, covering seventy thousand square kilometers. The river historically served as a major trade route and cultural artery, and dynasties like the Maurya and Gupta rose to power along its course. Today the river delta is experiencing severe ecological stress from pollution, damming, and climate change, with water levels fluctuating dangerously. Cremation of millions annually means human remains are routinely committed to the river in Hindu funeral practice.
